title: A buying group is never one person: the four personas to map
metaTitle: Buying group personas for IT firms
description: Most IT firms know the type of company they sell to, but often forget the four personas inside it: champion, approver, decision maker and influencer.
dek: Most IT firms have a good grip on the type of company they sell to. The people inside it are easier to forget, and I think there are four personas.
author: Shane Kennedy

shortVersion: I think there's four personas in an IT buying group: the champion, the approver, the decision maker and the influencer.
A lot of teams only speak to one of them and forget about the other three.
Map all four, ideally in your CRM, and write down what each of them wants and cares about.

beats.heading: The company, and the people in it
body: Most IT service businesses have a good grip on the type of company they sell to. Their industry, their size, their number of seats.
What they often forget about is the people inside those organisations: the buying group, and the personas they fit into.

beats.heading: The other three
body: I think there's four personas, and unfortunately a lot of teams only speak to one of them. They forget about the other three.
It's often the person who first got in touch. The proposal and every follow-up go to them, and the other three hear nothing aimed at them.

graphic.litLabel: The one a lot of teams talk to
graphic.dimLabel: The three who often get missed
graphic.caption: Illustration

beats.heading: The four personas
body: So have a think about this. Or even better, write it down.
The first persona is your champion. This is the person who sells on your behalf when you're not in the room.
The second is your approver, who signs off on the contract. It's often someone in finance or procurement.
Next is your decision maker, who's your IT manager or your application owner. Sometimes they're the same person as the champion.
And the fourth is the influencer. They're the frontline people who care about their life being easier, or about clicking a button and something happening.

items.title: Champion
items.text: Sells for you when you're not in the room

beats.heading: What each of them cares about
body: It's so important that you have these personas mapped, and even better in your CRM, and that you understand what each of them wants and cares about.

A champion needs something they can forward internally, like a short case study or a one-page summary. An approver's after the cost and the contract terms, laid out plainly. A decision maker's weighing you up against what the IT team has to get done this year. And an influencer wants to know what their day will look like once it's in.

body: Put each one against the deal in your CRM, so your next campaign can speak to all four.
